subject: Immediate: Token pipeline collapse — StratoBank reserved throughput breach
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@stratobank.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Srikanth Rao <srao@stratobank.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Sep 2026 08:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Production alert — token pipeline collapse, immediate impact

Jordan —

We’re seeing a sustained spike in 5xx and token queue depth for our production inference path since ~06:45 PT. Error rate climbed from 0.2% to ~7% and median latency for the LLM endpoint has jumped from 220ms -> 1.2s; customer-facing UI is timing out. This is a StratoBank high-impact workflow (loan decisioning).

Key things I pulled from our side:
- Failure patterns look like model node timeouts + request queue piling up; several errors reference KV cache misses.
- Our telemetry shows reserved qps consumption at 102% of committed capacity for last 40 minutes.
- Attaching a CSV and log excerpt.

We need a containment plan and ETA for remediation. Can you confirm whether this is a dedicated pool saturation or cross-tenant spill? We’re prepared to take a brief maintenance window if necessary but need an immediate mitigation path.

Elena
Elena Morales
Head of ML Platform, StratoBank
elena.morales@stratobank.com

Attachments: inference-metrics-20260923.csv; error-sample-logs.txt
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@stratobank.com>, Srikanth Rao <srao@stratobank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Sep 2026 15:24:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: Production alert — token pipeline collapse, immediate impact

Thanks for the alert, Elena — and sorry you’re hitting this. I’m escalating internally and pulling ops/infra now. Quick read: your metrics indicate reserved-capacity saturation on the dedicated GPU pool serving your model family.

Immediate actions we’re initiating (T+10):
- Marcus (infra) will re-route low-priority batch jobs off the dedicated pool and apply an emergency slot cap to free headroom.
- Tessa (customer ops) is starting a fast-fallback to a smaller quantized model variant to reduce token cost for priority routes.
- I’ll open an exec-level notify to Sales + Eng leadership since this is high-impact and there’s a reserved throughput breach.

Elena — can you confirm whether you have any on-prem batch windows running now? Also if you have a short list of the highest-volume routes we should prioritize for fallback, send that over and we’ll pin them.

Jordan
Jordan Blake
Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com

Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Sep 2026 16:03:00 +00:00
Subject: Fwd: Production alert — token pipeline collapse, immediate impact

Folks — looping in leadership. This is hitting StratoBank’s core decisioning flow; we need an exec-level containment & customer communication ASAP. Recommended immediate asks:

1) Marcus: prioritize power to StratoBank’s dedicated pool — apply emergency throttles to non-committed tenants and execute the slot cap Jordan mentioned. Provide ETA for durable headroom (target: <30 minutes).
2) Tessa / Jordan: Offer StratoBank an SLA credit & emergency burst authorization as we remediate; get signoff on customer message.
3) Priyom: prepare a short ‘what happened / mitigation / next steps’ readout for the CRO and for Legal if the customer requests contract remedies.

We should aim for a single coordinated customer update in 20–30 minutes. I’ll notify Sales leadership and the CTO that the incident is an active reserved-capacity breach.

Marissa Cole
VP, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Cc: Srikanth Rao <srao@stratobank.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Sep 2026 18:47:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: Production alert — token pipeline collapse, immediate impact

Jordan / Marissa —

Thank you for the rapid response and the mitigation steps. Update from our side: we took the fallback for the three highest-volume routes and error rate dropped to 0.9% in ~12 minutes; median latency improved to 360ms. We still see elevated queue depth relative to baseline but the customer UI is stable.

We need two things from Redwood:
- A short timeline for full recovery (when will dedicated pool return to baseline headroom without fallbacks).
- A post-incident write-up with root cause and long-term safeguards (we’re especially interested in KV cache behavior and routing policies that caused capacity to pin to your dedicated nodes).

Also, we will accept an emergency burst credit for the period of the incident. Please advise next steps and expected times for the follow-up doc.

Elena
